title: Finlay
body:
Finlay (formerly Finlay Island)

Finlay, or Finlay Island as it was once known, is the part of the map where all players can load their properties in. Beginner Tree Species and Rock Nodes spawn on the surface. Finlay also offers immediate access to a few beaches. The area also serves as the main junction connecting all the various locales that Oaklands offers.

Finlay provides eight different property plots for players to load in. After the Oaklands map update, player properties are now spaced apart, with a complete revamp of the starting area. They each have distinct advantages:

  • Plot 3 is the closest plot to almost everything in Oaklands, namely Ferwater and Snowy Peaks. It is especially nice due to its close location to the Resource Hub to quickly sell resources.
  • Plot 4 and Plot 5 are the closest plots to Snowy Peaks (and, consequently, the Icelands). Also quick access to Alan's Auto-Logistics.
  • Plot 1 and Plot 2 are placed in the center of the Grasslands, with quick access to Mike's Mines, the Oak Depot, and starter resources on Finlay.
  • Plot 6, 7, and 8 are often less contested due to their much farther distance from most relevant resources in the game, but they do have some small benefits:
    • Plot 6 has an alternate entrance to Mike's Mines and a Meteor Spawn location right in front of it. Also the closest plot to Alan's Auto-Logistics. Can access the Magma Caves quickly.
    • Plot 7 and Plot 8 are close to Flowering Meadows and the far side of the Finlay Taiga, so they are closer to the Acidlands. One of the plots has an alternate entrance to Mike's Mines too. Can access the Magma Caves quickly.

Notable Locations

Finlay Overview

Finlay is connected to areas that are completely unique - they are highly essential to progression:

  • Ferwater is a Savannah/Desert biome connected to Finlay by a bridge, which in turn allows access to the Desert Highlands and Uncertainty Cave.
  • Flowering Meadows is a grassy flower biome fused to Finlay, and you can easily drive inside from the mainland.
  • An entrance to Mike's Mines, a cave system located near player spawn, which in turn serves as the entrance to the Magma Caves.
  • An entrance to the Acidlands, a mid/late-game area, is located behind Flowering Meadows near the Lost Woods.
  • An entrance to the Snowy Peaks can be reached by travelling through the Finlay Taiga.
  • Several entrances to the River Caves, another separate cave system with a river spanning through it. They serve as a network of underground paths connecting disparate parts of the map together.

According to the brand new update, Finlay has been completely rehauled once more. Finlay can be subdivided into the following areas:

  • Finlay Grasslands
  • Finlay Taiga
  • Finlay Farlands
  • Finlay Beaches
  • Oak Forest/Mythril Forest
  • Birch Forest/Birch Ridge
  • Maple Forest
  • Olive Forest
  • Dark Forest/Lost Woods

Grasslands (Finlay)

  • Location of the Resource Hub and Oak Depot.
  • Has bright green grass.
  • Has several Player base spawn locations.

Oak Forest (Mythril Forest)

  • Also known as “Mythril Forest” according to signage.
  • Located just south of the Flowering Meadows entrance, or to the right of the Resource Hub.
  • Holds the remains of Jer’s Junkyard.
  • High spawn rate of Oak trees.
  • Despite the name sake, it is unlikely that Mythril spawns more commonly in this location.

Birch Forest (Birch Ridge)

  • Also known as "Birch Ridge" according to signage.
  • Located next to the bridge connecting Finlay to Ferwater and the smaller bridge that connects Finlay Grasslands to Finlay Taiga/Icelands.
  • High spawn rate of Birch trees.

Taiga (Finlay)

  • May also be referred to as Icelands to some players. Otherwise, Icelands is equivalent to Snowy Peaks.
  • Location of Alan’s Auto-Logistics.
  • Has cerulean, blue-green grass.
  • Has several Player base spawn locations.

Farlands (Finlay)

The Finlay Farlands (as named in the game using the map boards in Mike's Mines) is comprised of the area behind Flowering Meadows. This area contains Maple Forest, the two Olivewood Forests, the Lost Woods, and an entrance into the Acidlands.

  • Contains the Elderwood Axe Quest, in Lost Woods
  • Contains the hidden Emberbane quest, in an unmarked explodable wall near the back entrance of Flowering Meadows.

Maple Forest

  • Located between Flowering Meadows and the Finlay Taiga, stretches into the Acidlands Entrance.
  • High spawn rate of Red Maple trees.

Olive Forest

  • There are two Olivewood Forests in the Finlay Farlands: first located on a small plateau just outside of a second entrance of Flowering Meadows and second located on the cliff near the Lost Woods.
  • The only spawn location of Olivewood trees.

Dark Forest (Lost Woods)

  • Also also known as “Lost Woods” according to signage.
  • Located between Flowering Meadows and the Acidlands Entrance
  • Spawn location of Petrified Oak trees, along with a small lake.
  • Behind the waterfall is an exit from Mike's Mines.
  • The Elderbark Axe (early-game axe quest) can sometimes spawn on a Petrified Oak stump.

Beaches (Finlay)

With the new update, Finlay is now made up of several beaches - there are three distinct beaches shown on the map.

  • Grasslands Beach (South Finlay)
    • A beach south of Flowering Meadows.
    • Located near the Oak and Birch Forests.
    • Location of a “Shifting Realities” Portal frame to visit the retro map of Oaklands.
  • Farlands Beach (North Finlay)
    • A beach north of Flowering Meadows, which is connected with the beach inside Flowering Meadows.
    • Located near the Olive Forest, Maple Forest, and the Lost Woods.
    • Location of an entrance to Mike's Mines.
  • Finlay Taiga Beach
    • A beach formed from Finlay Taiga on its north side.
    • Location of the Radical Shack.
    • Spawns Grey Gravel nodes on the brown stone coastline.

Stores

Finlay Stores

Finlay offers several functions as the main hub of Oaklands. Finlay has the Resource Hub, which allows players to sell both processed and unprocessed goods. Finlay also contains five shops:

  • Oak Depot: sells all of the basic Schematics, all starter and professional processing machinery, early and mid-game vehicle spawners, various tools, and various items.
  • Alan’s Auto-Logistics: sells high-end vehicle spawners and logistical/electrical components.
  • Mike's Mines Shop: sells low-tier explosives.
  • Lighthouse: sells various specialty items, both decorational and functional, and 3 different sizes of Storage Crates.
  • Radical Shack: sells beach/ocean oriented items and the Living Axe.

Quests and Secrets

The land of Oaklands hides many secrets - some in plain sight, and others so obtuse that you will likely never find them without at least a hint. These secret puzzles offer powerful tools (some of the best in the game!). This offers a quick summary of secret quests that are active at least partially in Finlay, but note that most of these quests often require lots of resources, money, and map-wide navigation.

The Elderwood Axe

The Elderwood Axe is the easiest secret tool to obtain - and really should be the first quest item you look for when playing Oaklands for the first time. No need for any resources, no NPC's required, not even your truck is needed in any capacity.

  • This quest takes about 20 minutes (or less if you are lucky) to complete.
  • The Elderwood Axe spawns randomly on a Petrified Oak stump in the Lost Woods. Pick it up with at least one free inventory slot.
  • If one does not spawn, rejoin the game on a different server and check the Lost Woods again. Keep trying until you find one.

The Pedestal Puzzle

Finlay has two Pedestals, and Ferwater has one. The Pedestal Puzzle is used for the Uncertain Pickaxe and Adurite Key secret quests.

  • Pedestal 1 is located near the Lighthouse, in the center of the Lost Woods.
  • Pedestal 2 is located at the edge of a rock in front of Alan's Auto-Logistics.
  • Pedestal 3 is located in the center of the Desert Canyon in Ferwater.

In short, first press the secret Red Button in Mike's Mines to activate the Pedestal Puzzle - causing the pedestals themselves to have a glowing ring. Place ? ? ? (Infused Ink) on all three pedestals for the Uncertain Pickaxe. Place Refined Tools on all three pedestals for the Adurite Key. The quest item will spawn on another pedestal in the Acidlands.

  • The Pedestal Puzzle takes about 30 minutes to more than an hour to complete.
  • For more detail on the Undertain Pickaxe and Adurite Key quests, click on their respective links.

The Emberbane Quest

The Emberbane Ruins are located inside a hilltop on the way to the Lighthouse behind an unmarked wall which can be identified by its indent and its discoloration. It can be broken with explosives. This is the location to fuse a Meteor Core, a Burnt Skull, and an Adurite Key into one of the best Axes in Oaklands - the Emberbane Axe.

  • This quest takes more than a few hours to complete, requiring time, money, upgraded tools, explosives, luck, and lots of resources.
  • This Axe can also be bought with Robux by using the Expert Pack Gamepass.

Shifting Realities

The Shifting Realities portal frame is located on the Grasslands Beach - the beach near player spawn. By entering this mineshaft, eerily reminiscent of the original location of the Red Button, you can enter a bright green portal. By touching this portal, you will teleport to an Oaklands server with a retro version of the map. This map is the first version of the Oaklands map, with most of the original trappings. A few things, such as Kelp and the lack of Magma Trees near the retro Lighthouse, have been added and removed respectively.

  • This quest takes nearly no time to complete.
  • You will receive the "Shifting Realities" badge upon entering the retro server.

Lumberwork

Trees in Finlay Grasslands

Three default species of trees spawn on the Finlay Grasslands, with other species spawning in specific places on the surface of the island. These trees are the main tree species that spawn on Finlay, not including those that spawn via special events. These trees are mainly for beginners to earn money or to be used as a cheap building material. The trees that fall into this category are listed below:

  • Oak, common rarity, early-game tree, found across the Finlay Grasslands, spawns in clusters in the Oak Forest/Mithril Forest.
  • Birch, common rarity, early-game tree, found across the Finlay Grasslands, spawns in clusters in the Birch Forest.
  • Finlay Clover, uncommon rarity, early-game tree, found across all of the Finlay Grasslands. Only slightly more profitable than normal trees.

Trees near Flowering Meadows/Finlay Farlands

Near Flowering Meadows, several different tree types can be found. These trees are similarly for beginners to earn money or to be used as a cheap building material, but are a little bit beefier in terms of health. The following list describes these tree types:

  • Red Maple, common rarity, early-game tree, spawns in clusters in the Maple Forest, near the western side of Flowering Meadows.
  • Olivewood, common rarity (*but spawns in a specific area only), early/mid-game tree, found at a small plateau behind Flowering Meadows, near its second entrance or the entrance to the Acidlands.

Trees in Finlay Taiga

Across from Flowering Meadows is the Finlay Taiga, also known as Finlay Icelands. These trees are also mainly for beginners to earn money or to be used as a cheap building material, but are a little bit beefier in terms of health. The following describes these tree types:

  • Blue Pine, common rarity, early-game tree, found across the Finlay Taiga. Also found more sparsely in Snowy Peaks.
  • Spruce, common rarity, early-game tree, found across the Finlay Taiga. Also found more sparsely in Snowy Peaks.
  • Sequoia, common rarity (*but spawns in a specific area only), mid/late-game tree, found specifically near the small bridge entrance (close to the bridge to Ferwater) and towards the entrance to Snowy Peaks. Also found in hard to get areas in Snowy Peaks. Even though it is extremely large, its return value is relatively low compared to other, more profitable trees and has extremely high health. Can be processed for profit but will take a long time to transport, saw down into smaller chunks, process into planks, and sell it all - about $10K for a fully processed Sequoia. However, it is very useful for building as it can fill schematics easily with its larger mass.
  • Tundra Clover, uncommon rarity, early-game tree, found across all of the Finlay Taiga. Only slightly more profitable than normal trees.

Trees in Finlay Beaches

Some trees can only spawn on the beaches of Finlay. These trees are very low-value trees, likely implemented for decoration purposes - with the exception of the high-value Kelp. The trees that fall into this category are listed below:

  • Palm, common rarity, early-game tree, only on beach shores. Very low return value when selling - used for decorative and foraging purposes.
  • King Palm, common rarity, mid-game tree, only on beach shores. Being a very beefy tree like Sequoia, it is not recommended to cut down this tree and process it for profit. Unlike Sequoia, not as profitable due to its "smaller" comparative size. it is largely used for building and filling schematics.
  • Kelp, common rarity, early/mid-game tree, in the ocean near beach shores, useful to farm for early to mid-game money as it has a moderately high return value. Can be used to create "grass" or foliage in your builds when processed.

Trees in the Lost Woods

A new area that was in previous versions of Finlay has been reworked into an area called the Dark Forest. The sign at the entrance states that this area is named the Lost Woods, a sublocation on Finlay. This area is located near the entrance to the Acidlands, and it is very apparent when you enter it as it has a darker atmosphere and a lake. These trees are largely for building decoration because they have decent health (they are also protected by Skeleton and Zombie enemies!), so you should come later to this area if you want to use the wood-types here. The following describes these tree types:

  • Petrified Oak, common rarity (*but spawns in a specific area only), mid/late-game tree, found in the Lost Woods only. Only slightly more profitable than beginner trees, and with much higher health too. For building purposes - not farming money.
  • Red Mushroom, common rarity, mid-game tree, found in the Lost Woods but also in Uncertainty cave. Somewhat profitable with mild returns, but easier to farm than Kelp - a solid middle progression tree that does not compare against late-game trees. Also, relatively low health, so easier to farm for newer players.
  • Bamboo, common rarity, early/mid-game tree, found near lake shores, including the lake in the Lost Woods. Somewhat profitable with mild returns, but smaller overall size makes it less ideal to farm than other trees. Very low health, so an early-to-mid-game tree that offers some money. However, it is used mostly for its cool building materials.

Special and Event Trees

Special types of trees can spawn during special events - typically describing a random weather event. Only Thunderstorm event trees are active at this time in Finlay. If you want to see meteor locations, see the updated Map of Finlay on the wiki! The trees that fall into this category are listed below:

  • Magma Tree, rare rarity, late-game tree, appears at Meteor impact sites in numbers of 2-5, but can also spawn in the Magma Caves naturally. High health, but also high-return value, sell processed for large profit.
  • Ash Tree, uncommon rarity, late-game tree, appears at Meteor impact sites in numbers of 2-5, but can also spawn in the Magma Caves naturally. Not nearly as profitable as Magma Trees, but can be used as a dark material in builds.
  • Electrified Tree, uncommon rarity, tree variant, mid/late-game tree, appears during thunderstorms upon lightning striking any type of tree. Can spawn in an Electrified Meteor. High-return value, sell processed for large profit.
  • Electrified Bamboo, uncommon rarity, tree variant, mid/late-game tree, appears during thunderstorms upon lightning striking Bamboo near Ook Lake or in the Lost woods lake. Can spawn in an Electrified Meteor. High-return value, sell processed for large profit.
  • Eel Kelp, uncommon rarity, tree variant, mid/late-game tree, appears during thunderstorms upon lightning striking Kelp in the ocean. Can spawn in an Electrified Meteor. High-return value, sell processed for large profit.

Finlay Lumberwork Summary

For a quick at-a-glance explanation on the rarities and difficulties for obtaining each resource in Oaklands. Note that these are not official in any capacity and are listed to help you estimate which resource you would want to farm or use in your builds!

Rarity Explanation
Common Spawns commonly, low sell value, and typically spawns in easy-to-reach areas.
Uncommon Spawns less frequently, but not particularly rare. Can have decent sell value, or might only spawn in specific areas.
Rare May spawn rarely, can only spawn under certain conditions, has high sell value, or spawns in particularly hard to reach areas.
Unique Is given if a special action is required to obtain it, not necessarily rare or lucrative. Usually for quests.
Difficulty Explanation
Very Easy Extremely common, near to the point of effortlessness to find and farm.
Easy Common, may even be extremely common, but may be harder to farm in large quantities.
Low Medium Common, but it spawns in a specific location that makes it harder to farm in large quantities, or is difficult to transport,
Medium Spawns in a specific location that requires certain tools or is generally a nuisance to farm.
High Medium Spawns in a specific location that requires certain tools and is difficult to transport or is located far away from base.
Difficult Does not have a guaranteed spawn area, requires certain conditions to spawn, requires certain tools. Not possible to farm in large quantities in a short time frame.
Unobtainable Is no longer in the game or its method of obtaining has been removed.
Event Appears for a holiday or special event, such as St. Patricks or Oaklands Anniversary.
Varies For some reason, the difficulty to obtain it can change drastically.

Mining

To Wiki Editors: Make sure the info you list is relevant for Finlay. For example: Iron can spawn on Lightslate (put this in). However, Iron can also spawn on Blueslate (this stone type can NOT spawn on Finlay, so don't put it in).

Finlay Stone Types

Due to an update with with ore and stone generation, much of the information of ores and stones remain outdated. Here is the up-to-date guide on mining in Finlay up to the major revamp of the Finlay Map. Mining is classified into two main categories: stone types and ore types. See the Ore page for a list of all stone and ore types. Ores can only spawn in certain stone nodes. The following is a list of stone nodes that can spawn in Finlay:

  • Beigeslate, common rarity, early-game stone, found near everywhere in Oaklands.
  • Lightslate, common rarity, early-game stone, found near everywhere in Oaklands.
  • Darkslate, common rarity, early-game stone, frequent but spawns in certain areas in Finlay.
  • Smokeslate, common rarity, early-game stone, frequent but spawns in certain areas in Finlay.
  • Marble, common rarity, early-game stone, frequent but spawns in certain areas in Finlay.
  • Sandstone, common rarity, early-game stone, spawns on any normal beach.
  • Greygravel, common rarity, early-game stone, only spawns at the Finlay Taiga Beach shores (alternatively, where the Radical Shack is located)
  • Blue, Red, and Brown Clay, common rarity, early/mid-game stone, only spawns underwater near specific areas, typically coastlines.

Finlay Ore Types

Ores spawn in a particular stone type. Due to an update to the way in which ores and stone nodes are generated, different ores can not spawn on the same node - for example, Pyrite can not spawn on Lightslate. Using a Metal Detector allows you to easily identify what ore, if any, occupies a stone node. This is a comprehensive list of all ores that could spawn in Finlay disregarding glitches:

  • Copper, common rarity, found in Beigeslate.
  • Pyrite, common rarity, found in Beigeslate.
  • Gold, common rarity, found in Beigeslate (low spawn rate in Finlay; higher spawn rate in Mike’s Mines).
  • Iron, common rarity, found in Lightslate.
  • Ink, common rarity, found in Lightslate.
  • Magnetite, rare rarity, found in Lightslate, spawn at a rate of 0.1% or 1/1000 chance at night only. Stays present in the day until the node disappears normally. Glows purple, so it is very identifiable. Worth more trading than its base sell value - keep it to trade!
  • Tin, common rarity, in Darkslate.
  • Mythril, uncommon rarity, found in Darkslate and Smokeslate (low spawn rate in Finlay; higher spawn rate in Mike’s Mines)
  • Lithium, common rarity, in Smokeslate.
  • Quartz, common rarity, in Marble.
  • Rosa Flama Quartz, uncommon rarity, in Marble.
  • Sand, common rarity, in Sandstone.
  • Blue, Red, and Brown Opal, uncommon rarity, in Blue, Red, and Brown Clay (low spawn rate in normal waters; guaranteed spawn in Desert Oasis and certain areas of the River Caves)
  • Electrified Rock, uncommon rarity, stone variant, spawned by a thunderstorm on the surface, or by a lightning strike on any stone node using Michael’s Copper Axe.

Foraging

**NEED HELP TO KNOW IF THESE ARE ALL THE FORAGEABLES. If you do not see one that should be here, please feel free to add them! Thanks! 

**Missing Tree Burls, a rare forage item found on (seemingly?) any tree and is specific to that tree (e.g. an oak tree burl).

Disclaimer to Wiki Editors: Do NOT add if found only in Flowering Meadows! (i.e. tulips)

Foraging in Finlay

There are several flowers and miscellaneous items that can be picked up from all over Finlay. Most of these items can be composted and turned into dirt using the Composter. They can also be pressed into jams (for fruits) and dyes (for flowers/other forage items) using the Press Machine and a Jar. Both can be used as decoration items. Jams can be sold at a much higher profit than raw foraged items, and dyes can be used to change wire colors. Most forage items are not worth selling, unless processed (except for a raw Golden Apple, and that should be processed to maximize profit). Most forageables are not worth very much - if you plan to farm with jams/dyes, you should pick a forageable with a high selling rate that is not so annoying to get. As a whole, they should be used as decoration - or for their unique colors. Finlay has plentiful foraging items, but most of them are common rarity. The following is a comprehensive list of all the forageable items that can be found in this area.

Ground Foraging

Certain forage items in Finlay only spawn on the ground without any bush, tree, or log to sprout from. These forage items are almost always extremely common and are largely used for their dye color. They are also not worth selling compared to selling processed lumber and minerals. Ground forage items that are found in Finlay are listed here:

  • Green Mums, common rarity, anywhere on grassy ground in Finlay Grasslands.
  • Daisies, common rarity, anywhere on grassy ground in Finlay Grasslands.
  • Dandelions, common rarity, anywhere on grassy ground in Finlay Grasslands.
  • Lucky Clovers, common rarity, on grassy ground anywhere in Finlay Grasslands.
  • Blue Cornflowers, common rarity, on on grassy ground near Snowy Peaks entrance in the Finlay Taiga, and in select areas of Finlay Taiga.
  • Nightshade, common rarity, on on grassy ground in the wooded area of the Lost Woods.
  • Cattails, common rarity, on sandy or grassy ground in areas surrounding the lake of the Lost Woods.
  • Lavender, common rarity, most often spawn on grassy ground in or around the Finlay Farlands.

Bush Foraging

Certain forage items spawn on bushes and are easier to see. They are typically flowers or fruits that, like ground forageables, can be composted or pressed. Bush forage items that are found in Finlay are listed here:

  • Hydrangeas (White/Purple/Pink/Green/Blue), common rarity, from any normal bush in Finlay Grasslands.
  • Blueberries, common rarity, from most bushes in Finlay Grasslands.
  • Cranberries, common rarity, from most bushes in Finlay Taiga.
  • Grapes, common rarity, from some bushes in Finlay Grasslands, and from bushes in the Finlay Farlands near Flowering Meadows. Grapes can also spawn hanging on the foliage of the stone archways.

Tree Foraging

Certain forage items spawn on trees and are sometimes visible on the leaves of the tree. If the tree is cut down, the forage items can still be picked up. There is a percent chance that the forage item will rot and disappear if using a regular Axe. However, forage items are guaranteed not to rot if you pick them by hand or use the Living Axe. They are typically seeds or fruits that, like other forageables, can be composted or pressed. Tree forage items that are found in Finlay are listed here:

  • Acorns, common rarity, from Oak trees.
  • Apples, common rarity, from Oak trees.
  • Golden Apples, rare rarity, forage variant, 1/1000 chance to replace an apple, from Oak trees.
  • Pears, common rarity, from Birch trees.
  • Pinecones, common rarity, from Blue Pine trees.
  • Sap, common rarity, from Red Maple trees and detritus.
  • Coconuts, common rarity, from Palm trees and across the beach floor.
  • Bananas, common rarity, from King Palm trees.
  • Olives, common rarity, from Olivewood trees.

  • Tree Burls, rare rarity, forage variant, rare chance to spawn on any tree with wood.

Miscellaneous Foraging

Certain forage items have unique spawn conditions. This includes mushrooms that spawn on tree bark and fallen trees/stumps (detritus). Others must have water to spawn on or have strange spawn conditions. Like other forageables, can be composted or pressed. Miscellaneous forage items that are found in Finlay are listed here:

  • Beehives, uncommon rarity, from tree leaves whilst using a Saw. Can be sanded into Honeycomb and pressed into Honey.
  • Agaric Mushrooms, common rarity, from several tree bark types, on several types of tree detritus, and from the ground.
  • Daedalea Mushrooms, common rarity, from several tree bark types and Oak tree detritus.
  • Cremini Mushrooms, common rarity, from Blue Pine trees and Blue Pine detritus.
  • Black Truffles, uncommon rarity, sparsely spawns on the ground in the Lost Woods.
  • Celestial Flowers, common rarity, from foliage in a cave and under a wooden bridge in the Lost Woods. Also found in Flowering Meadows and Mike's Mines.
  • Pink Lotus, common rarity, from the lake in Lost Woods, or from the river flowing above it. Found in most lakes and rivers across the map.
  • Water Lily, common rarity, from the lake in Lost Woods, or from the river flowing above it. Found in most lakes and rivers across the map.

Event or Weather Foraging

Certain forage items have unique spawn conditions. This includes spawning only at night, falling from the sky, or rarer events like Meteors. Seasonal foraging (E.g. ghosts (firefly reskin), St. Patrick's day, moon shards from Halloween, etc.) can also be included here. 

Star Chances need testing for confirmation. Star chances and weather event calculations are estimated.
  • Stars (Yellow/Green/Red/Blue/Purple), common rarity, forage variant, spawn anywhere in Finlay at night.
  • Fireflies (Yellow/Green/Red/Blue/Purple), common rarity, forage variant, spawn anywhere in Finlay at night.
    • Yellow, common rarity, has a ~84% or ~8/10 spawn chance.
    • Green, common rarity, has a 10% or 1/10 spawn chance.
    • Red, common rarity, has a 5% or 1/20 spawn chance.
    • Blue, uncommon rarity, has a 0.9% or roughly ~1/100 spawn chance
    • Purple, rare rarity, is the rarest variant. Has a <0.1% or 1/1000 spawn chance.
  • Note that the frequency of star spawns depend upon the weather:
    • During stormy conditions (such as rainy or thunderstorm), star spawning is reduced by about 0.5X.
    • A clear night has a 1/5 chance to be a star shower, where stars spawn 2X more than usual.
  • Meteor Core, uncommon rarity, 100% spawn chance from both a Magmafied Meteor and an Electrified Meteor. Used for special quests.

Removed Assets

Special Event Items

These items are no longer in game, whether due to a game update or a special event. As an example, these items have been removed from Finlay; they used to appear on April Fools and Oaklands Anniversary events. However, retro items are now a permanent addition to Oaklands as resources found in the Classic Biome.

  • Tree (Retro)
  • Stone (Retro)
  • Ore (Retro)

Removed Locations

These locations are no longer in the game since the Oaklands map update - their functions have either been reused in other assets/locations or removed entirely in the Main Oaklands servers. However, they are still accessible by using the Shifting Realities portal frame found at Finlay Beach.

  • Jer's Junkyard (Retro Version) - a dilapidated version of the junkyard is now in Mythril Forest.
  • Mike's Mines (Retro Version) - has been remade into a much more expansive cave system.
  • Ook Lake (Retro Version) - has be re-added to the game in Ferwater instead.

Trivia

  • Finlay Island was the first island to be added to the game.
  • The Lighthouse on Finlay used to be broken in half and served as the spawn for Magma Trees; after the map update, the Lighthouse returned to its former glory and as a result no longer spawns Magma Trees.
  • After the map update, Jer's Junkyard and its functions have been split into two locations. The Resource Hub is now the area to sell goods and Jer's Junk has now been set up outside the Lighthouse.
  • Players used to be able to sell their materials at the Oak Depot, but this feature has been removed in favor of the Resource Hub.
  • The Classic Store used to be on Finlay before being moved to Ferwater in the island expansion update. Currently, the Classic Store is in the Classic Biome from a following update.
